writtenTo: The people of Judah and Jerusalem
importantNotes: Isaiah is sometimes called 'the Fifth Gospel' because of its detailed messianic prophecies.
Isaiah 53 describes the suffering of Christ in remarkable detail — written 700 years before the cross.
The book has 66 chapters mirroring the Bible's 66 books: chs. 1-39 (judgment) and 40-66 (comfort).
'Holy, holy, holy' (6:3) — the only attribute of God repeated three times in Scripture.
Isaiah prophesied for about 60 years during the reigns of four kings of Judah.

chapters.1: God indicts Judah for rebellion and empty worship; a call to repentance.
chapters.2: The future glory of Zion; judgment on human pride and idolatry.
chapters.3: Judgment on Jerusalem's leaders and the proud women of Zion.
chapters.4: The Branch of the LORD — a remnant will be holy and protected.
chapters.5: The Song of the Vineyard — Judah has produced bad fruit; six woes.
chapters.6: Isaiah's vision of God's glory in the Temple; his call and commission.
chapters.7: The sign of Immanuel — 'a virgin will conceive' — spoken to King Ahaz.
chapters.8: Warnings about Assyria; fear God, not man; the coming darkness.
chapters.9: The promise of a Child: 'Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.'
chapters.10: Woe to unjust rulers; Assyria is God's instrument but will be judged; the remnant will return.
chapters.11: The Branch from Jesse — the Messiah's peaceful kingdom; the wolf with the lamb.
chapters.12: A song of praise and thanksgiving for God's salvation.
chapters.13: Oracle against Babylon — the day of the LORD is coming.
chapters.14: The fall of the king of Babylon; taunt against the fallen tyrant.
chapters.15: Oracle against Moab — destruction and mourning.
chapters.16: Moab's desolation continues; a plea for justice and the throne of David.
chapters.17: Oracle against Damascus and Israel — judgment is coming.
chapters.18: Oracle against Cush (Ethiopia) — distant nations will bring tribute to God.
chapters.19: Oracle against Egypt — judgment followed by future blessing and worship.
chapters.20: Isaiah walks naked as a sign of Egypt and Cush's coming shame.
chapters.21: Oracles against Babylon, Edom (Dumah), and Arabia.
chapters.22: Oracle against Jerusalem ('Valley of Vision') — judgment for complacency.
chapters.23: Oracle against Tyre — the great trading city will be destroyed.
chapters.24: The LORD will devastate the earth — a global judgment and the triumph of God.
chapters.25: A song of praise — God will swallow up death forever; He will wipe away tears.
chapters.26: A song of trust — 'You will keep in perfect peace those whose minds are steadfast.'
chapters.27: The LORD will punish Leviathan; Israel will flourish like a vineyard.
chapters.28: Woe to Ephraim; the precious cornerstone in Zion; judgment on scoffers.
chapters.29: Woe to Jerusalem (Ariel); the people honor God with lips but not hearts.
chapters.30: Woe to those who rely on Egypt instead of God; God's grace to those who wait.
chapters.31: Woe to those who trust in horses and chariots instead of the LORD.
chapters.32: The righteous king; judgment on complacent women; the Spirit will be poured out.
chapters.33: The LORD rises up; He will be the stability of Zion and its judge.
chapters.34: The LORD's judgment on all nations, especially Edom.
chapters.35: The ransomed shall return to Zion with singing — the desert will bloom.
chapters.36: Sennacherib of Assyria invades Judah and threatens Jerusalem.
chapters.37: Hezekiah prays; Isaiah prophesies deliverance; an angel destroys the Assyrian army.
chapters.38: Hezekiah's illness and prayer; God adds 15 years to his life.
chapters.39: Hezekiah shows his treasures to Babylonian envoys; Isaiah predicts the Babylonian exile.
chapters.40: 'Comfort, comfort my people' — God's glory, power, and tenderness; soaring on wings like eagles.
chapters.41: God is with Israel; fear not — I am your God; I will strengthen you.
chapters.42: The Servant of the LORD — gentle, just, a light to the nations.
chapters.43: 'Fear not, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.'
chapters.44: God alone is the Creator; the folly of idol worship; Cyrus named as deliverer.
chapters.45: God commissions Cyrus; there is no God beside the LORD; every knee will bow.
chapters.46: The idols of Babylon are burdens; the LORD carries His people from birth to old age.
chapters.47: The fall of Babylon — her pride and sorcery will not save her.
chapters.48: Israel's stubbornness; God refines His people; 'Leave Babylon!'
chapters.49: The Servant of the LORD speaks; God will restore Israel and be a light to the Gentiles.
chapters.50: The Servant's obedience amid suffering — He sets His face like flint.
chapters.51: Look to Abraham; awake, Zion! The LORD comforts and redeems His people.
chapters.52: Zion, awake and put on beautiful garments; the Servant will be exalted.
chapters.53: The Suffering Servant — He was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities.
chapters.54: Sing, O barren woman! God's everlasting love and covenant of peace.
chapters.55: Come, all who are thirsty! Seek the LORD while He may be found.
chapters.56: Salvation for foreigners and eunuchs; God's house is for all nations.
chapters.57: The righteous perish unnoticed; condemnation of idolatry; peace for the humble.
chapters.58: True fasting — justice, mercy, and compassion, not empty ritual.
chapters.59: Sin separates from God; the Redeemer will come to Zion.
chapters.60: Arise, shine! The glory of the LORD rises upon Zion; nations come to her light.
chapters.61: The Spirit of the LORD is upon me — good news, freedom, and the year of the LORD's favor.
chapters.62: Zion's future glory — she will be a crown of splendor in the LORD's hand.
chapters.63: The LORD as warrior; a prayer recalling God's past mercies and Israel's rebellion.
chapters.64: A prayer for God to come down and act; 'We are the clay, you are the potter.'
chapters.65: New heavens and new earth — God creates a new reality of joy and peace.
chapters.66: Final judgment and glory — all nations will see God's splendor; new heavens and new earth.
